instruction: In VLC's preferences, raise the maximum volume amplification to 200%.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter (get_vlc_config) correctly reads ~/.config/vlc/vlcrc on Linux, which is the right file for VLC preferences including qt-max-volume.
Metric (check_qt_max_volume) correctly accesses rule['expected_qt_max_volume'] directly, consistent with type='rule' framework behavior where the rules dict is passed as 'rule'.
Expected value '200' matches the instruction's requirement of 200% maximum volume amplification.
Postconfig kills VLC before reading the config file, correctly forcing VLC to flush its settings to disk.
Default value '125' (VLC's factory default) ensures the initial state fails, providing negative-control resistance.
Single-requirement instruction is fully covered by the single evaluator check.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: The line matching 'qt-max-volume=' in line does not skip commented lines (e.g., '#qt-max-volume=125'). Adding a check to skip lines starting with '#' would be more robust, though in practice the active setting line will appear after any comment and overwrite the matched value correctly.
